extracted.intended_audience: journalists, newsroom editors, journalism students, and media professionals
extracted.subtask_description: A concise statement of the core ethical and professional principles that should guide reporting and newsroom practice, including purpose, verification, independence, public service, and responsibilities of citizens. Useful for editorial policy, journalism training, and evaluating journalistic work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The central purpose of journalism is to provide citizens with accurate and reliable information they need to function in a free society. This includes defining community, creating common language and knowledge, identifying community goals/heroes/villains, pushing people beyond complacency, being entertaining, serving as watchdog and offering voice to the voiceless.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalism's purpose encompasses multiple roles; work should prioritize information that helps citizens act in a free society. This framing implies that stories should be relevant to civic life, provide context, and serve public needs rather than solely commercial or entertainment aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalism's first obligation is to the truth
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalism must pursue a practical, journalistic truth by assembling and verifying facts and conveying a fair, reliable account of their meaning, valid for now and subject to further investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verification is central: assemble facts, verify them, provide context and interpretation, be transparent about sources and methods so audiences can assess information. Accuracy underpins context, analysis, and debate; truth emerges over time through continual inquiry. Avoid presenting unverified claims as fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Its first loyalty is to citizens
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists must maintain allegiance to citizens and the larger public interest above other constituencies (advertisers, shareholders), providing news without fear or favor and presenting a representative picture of all constituent groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News organizations and business units should nurture, not exploit, allegiance to audiences. Coverage should avoid disenfranchising groups by omission or bias; credibility is built by serving citizens first. Beware of slanting coverage for friends or advertisers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Its essence is a discipline of verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalism relies on a professional discipline for verifying information — a consistent method of testing evidence so personal and cultural biases do not undermine accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Techniques include seeking multiple witnesses, disclosing source information, asking various sides for comment, and using transparent methods. Objectivity refers to method, not absence of bias. Journalism should develop better systems for testing reliability of interpretation as well as facts. Avoid accepting single uncorroborated accounts and opaque sourcing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Its practitioners must maintain an independence from those they cover
rubrics_metrics.description: Independence of spirit and mind is required; credibility stems from accuracy, intellectual fairness and ability to inform rather than devotion to a group or outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independence does not mean neutrality in all forms (editorialists may take positions) but requires resisting ties that compromise reporting. Avoid arrogance, elitism, isolation or nihilism. Disclose conflicts of interest and ensure coverage decisions are not influenced by subjects of reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: It must serve as an independent monitor of power
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalism has a special role as watchdog over those whose power most affects citizens; this protects democracy and must not be demeaned or exploited for commercial gain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursue scrutiny of public and private power, protect watchdog freedom, and avoid using investigative authority frivolously or for profit motives that dilute the watchdog role.

rubrics_metrics.name: It must provide a forum for public criticism and compromise
rubrics_metrics.description: The news media are carriers of public discussion and should inform that discussion with facts, fairly represent varied viewpoints, place them in context, and not highlight only conflicting fringes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foster informed debate that emphasizes common ground where problem solving occurs. Coverage should aim to represent diverse interests and avoid amplifying only extreme voices or partisan flashpoints. Contextualize disagreements and present constructive avenues for compromise.

rubrics_metrics.name: It must strive to make the significant interesting and relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalism is storytelling with purpose; it must balance audience desires with what they need, making important subjects engaging so work both enlightens and engages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuously ask what information has most value to citizens and in what form. Avoid trivializing coverage or giving false significance to unimportant matters. Measure effectiveness by both engagement and enlightenment.

rubrics_metrics.name: It must keep the news comprehensive and proportional
rubrics_metrics.description: News should be kept in proportion and not omit important things; journalism creates a 'map' for citizens to navigate society, so inflating events, neglecting others, stereotyping, or disproportionate negativity undermines reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for comprehensiveness across communities and topics; diversify newsroom backgrounds and perspectives to avoid blind spots. Recognize that proportion and comprehensiveness are subjective but essential; avoid sensation, neglect, and stereotyping in coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Its practitioners must be allowed to exercise their personal conscience
rubrics_metrics.description: Every journalist must have a personal sense of ethics and responsibility — a moral compass — and be willing to voice differences with colleagues when fairness and accuracy require it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: News organizations should encourage individuals to speak their minds to foster intellectual diversity necessary for accurate coverage. Support dissenting voices internally when they serve accuracy and fairness; nurture ethical debate rather than suppress it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizens' rights and responsibilities regarding the news
rubrics_metrics.description: Citizens have rights and responsibilities when it comes to the news (added in 2007 revision of The Elements of Journalism).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that the information ecosystem requires active, informed citizens as well as responsible journalism. Encourage media literacy, critical consumption, and civic engagement; avoid treating audiences as passive consumers.
